papers.title: How Much Do You Trust A Dog? Quantifying Hint-Following in Reasoning Language Models
papers.summary: Large language models (LLMs) often exhibit sycophancy, altering their answers to align with user suggestions even on objective factual and reasoning tasks. Yet the quantitative form of this influence--- and whether it is calibrated to source reliability--- remains poorly understood. In this work, we investigate this behavior through hint-induced answer shifts on MMLU questions, evaluating prompts of the form ``[Source] thinks the answer is (X)''. We systematically vary the source to which the hint is attributed (a professor, a friend, or a dog) across three open-source model families, Qwen, Gemma, and SmolLM. We show that the change induced by the hint follows a predictable structure well-characterized by an exponential tilt: the hint induces an approximately constant mean shift in the hinted answer's log-odds, with question--target susceptibility largely shared across sources. To explore how this pattern can arise, we introduce a formal decomposition of the hint response and illustrate in controlled synthetic experiments how KL-regularized reward-based training reshapes both hinted and unhinted answer distributions. Finally, we evaluate whether this shift is calibrated to source reliability, finding that the log-odds shift persists even when the hint-giver is declared inaccurate or accompanied by explicit warnings not to trust the source, highlighting the vulnerability of LLMs to adversarial steering.
papers.title_ja: 犬をどの程度信頼するか？推論言語モデルにおけるヒント追従の定量化
papers.summary_ja: 大規模言語モデル（LLM）がユーザーの提案やヒントに対して迎合的に回答を変える現象（サコファンシー）を、MMLU問題を用いて定量的に分析した。プロンプト内の情報源（教授、友人、犬など）を変化させ、ヒントによる回答の確率分布への影響を評価した。その結果、ヒントは回答の対数オッズにほぼ一定の平均シフトをもたらし、この感受性は情報源の種類を問わず共通していることが判明した。さらに、情報源が不正確であると明示してもシフトは持続し、LLMが敵対的な誘導に対して脆弱であることが示された。
papers.relevance_reason: LLMの推論特性とハルシネーション・信頼性評価に直結する

papers.title: PrefO2O: Zero-Shot Preference-Based Reinforcement Learning via Offline-to-Online Latent Preference Transfer
papers.summary: Preference-based reinforcement learning (PbRL) has emerged as a promising paradigm for learning robot behaviors aligned with human intent. However, its scalability is fundamentally limited by the need to collect expensive human preference labels for every new task. In this work, we present PrefO2O, an offline-to-online latent preference transfer framework that enables zero-shot PbRL on unseen target tasks without requiring any human feedback. The core idea is to learn a task-invariant latent preference space from a small amount of offline preference data on source tasks, where transferable preference structures are disentangled from task-specific variations. This learned manifold allows PrefO2O to transfer preference structures and reward priors to new tasks under distribution shift, while confidence-weighted optimal transport alignment generates reliable pseudo-preference supervision for online reward adaptation. Extensive experiments on robotic manipulation and locomotion benchmarks demonstrate that PrefO2O substantially outperforms existing preference-transfer baselines and matches or exceeds PbRL methods trained with real human feedback, while generalizing across multi-to-one and one-to-one transfer settings as well as across different robot embodiments.
papers.title_ja: PrefO2O: オフラインからオンラインへの潜在好意転送によるゼロショット好意ベース強化学習
papers.summary_ja: 本論文は、人間のフィードバックなしで新しいタスクに対応できる好意ベース強化学習（PbRL）フレームワーク「PrefO2O」を提案する。ソースタスクのオフラインデータからタスク不変な潜在好意空間を学習し、分布シフト下でも好意構造と報酬事前分布をターゲットタスクへ転送する。信頼度重み付き最適輸送アライメントを用いて疑似好意監督信号を生成し、オンライン報酬適応を行う。ロボット操作や歩行のベンチマークにおいて、既存の好意転送手法を上回り、実人間のフィードバックを用いたPbRLと同等以上の性能を示した。
papers.relevance_reason: 強化学習と報酬設計の効率化が関心領域と一致

papers.title: SEVI: Safe Evidential Real-World Reinforcement Learning
papers.summary: Real-world reinforcement learning has enabled contact-rich manipulation tasks to be trained directly on physical robots, but unsafe interactions during online learning remain a key barrier to practical deployment. We propose Safe Evidential Real-World Reinforcement Learning (SEVI), a framework for reliability-aware safety intervention during real-world policy learning. SEVI introduces an Evidential Safety Critic that estimates both future constraint-violation risk and epistemic uncertainty in a single forward pass. During online learning, SEVI evaluates each task-policy action before execution; if the action is predicted to be unsafe or the prediction is insufficiently supported by evidence, SEVI overrides it with an offline-trained recovery policy that guides the robot toward a lower-risk region. We evaluate SEVI on two simulated manipulation tasks and a real-world USB insertion task under in-distribution and distribution-shifted conditions. Across task-learning and safety-critic baselines, SEVI achieves the strongest trajectory-level safety prediction, the highest final task success, and the lowest unsafe-event counts. SEVI also reduces unsafe events by 13.4 to 57.1 percent relative to recovery-based safe RL while preserving low-latency execution-time filtering. The project page is available at: https://sevi-safe.github.io/
papers.title_ja: SEVI: 安全な証拠ベースの実世界強化学習
papers.summary_ja: 実世界での強化学習における安全性と信頼性を高めるためのフレームワークSEVIを提案する。証拠ベースのセーフティクリティクを用い、単一のフォワードパスで将来の制約違反リスクと認識的不確実性を同時に推定する。オンライン学習中、アクションが不安全または証拠が不十分と判断された場合、オフライン学習済みのリカバリーポリシーで上書きし、低リスク領域へ誘導する。シミュレーションおよび実機USB挿入タスクにおいて、既存手法比で不安全イベントを最大57.1%削減しつつ、高いタスク成功率と低遅延を実現した。
papers.relevance_reason: 強化学習と不確実性推定が関心領域に合致

papers.title: Effectiveness of Curriculum Learning Depends on Reward Sparsity and Competing Optima
papers.summary: While animals and people tend to learn a task more quickly and reliably when they first train on simpler versions of it, curriculum learning's effectiveness in artificial settings varies, and appears substantially greater in reinforcement learning than in supervised learning. In this work, we construct and analyze a minimal model of policy learning to better understand why. We consider an open-loop, episodic target interception task whose parameters---especially how close the agent must be to the target to receive an informative reward signal---can be chosen so that the agent either receives informative rewards frequently ('dense' rewards) or rarely ('sparse' rewards). We mathematically and numerically analyze the dynamics of REINFORCE-based policy learning in both cases. In the dense reward case, curricula have only marginal benefits; in the sparse case, curricula can be required for learning to occur at all. We find that this is especially true when the agent has the conflicting goals of minimizing effort and accumulating high reward, since this can produce distinct reward landscape optima which compete with one another. Our characterization of useful curricula in this setting indicates that they address two issues: they (i) make rewards less sparse to speed up learning, and (ii) shape the reward landscape to steer agents away from bad local optima.
papers.title_ja: カリキュラム学習の有効性は報酬の疎性と競合する最適解に依存する
papers.summary_ja: 強化学習におけるカリキュラム学習の有効性を、報酬の疎性と競合する最適解の観点から分析した。オープンループのエピソード型ターゲット追跡タスクにおいて、REINFORCEベースのポリシー学習のダイナミクスを数学的・数値的に解析した。報酬が密な場合はカリキュラムの効果が限定的だが、報酬が疎な場合は学習成立に必須であることが示された。特に努力最小化と報酬最大化が競合し、悪い局所最適解が生まれる場合、カリキュラムは報酬を密にしつつ報酬景観を整形することで学習を促進する。
papers.relevance_reason: 強化学習の手法全般およびエージェント設計の基礎理論に深く関連するため

papers.title: Heterogeneous Space Data Centers: A Key Paradigm for Future Non-Terrestrial and In-Orbit Services
papers.summary: Lower space-launch cost and advances in AI are driving space-based data centers (SDCs) that provide AI-centric computing and communication services to in-orbit and non-terrestrial assets. However, architectural principles, service models, and energy provisioning for such SDCs, particularly in low-Earth orbit (LEO), remain largely unexplored. We introduce heterogeneous SDCs composed of large and small nodes, differentiated by computing capability, size, and power budget, to support applications spanning ground, aerial, and in-orbit users. We define use cases, node sizing and placement strategies, and interconnection topologies integrating space-to-space and space-to-ground links. Focusing on dawn-dusk LEO configurations, we analyze solar power availability, visibility windows, and latency-aware coverage. Using baseline workloads for typical scenarios, we evaluate latency and service reliability. We quantify energy requirements of different SDC roles and deployment scales, highlighting trade-offs among node size, orbit selection, and service portfolio, and provide design guidance and future research directions for AI infrastructure in space.
papers.title_ja: 異種構成の宇宙データセンター：将来の非地上・軌道上サービスのための主要パラダイム
papers.summary_ja: 低コストな打ち上げとAI技術の進歩を背景に、軌道上や非地上資産向けにAI計算・通信サービスを提供する宇宙データセンター（SDC）のアーキテクチャを提案する。計算能力や電力予算が異なる大規模・小規模ノードからなる異種構成のSDCを定義し、LEO（低軌道）におけるノード配置、接続トポロジー、および太陽光発電の可用性を分析する。さらに、典型的なワークロードを用いてレイテンシとサービス信頼性を評価し、ノードサイズ、軌道選択、サービスポートフォリオ間のトレードオフを定量化することで、宇宙におけるAIインフラ設計の指針を示す。

papers.title: Neural LoFi with Backward Coupling: A Spectral Theory of Cross-Layer Feature Learning
papers.summary: During joint training, backpropagation allows later layers to reshape earlier representations, a feedback mechanism absent from purely layer-wise learning. We extend Neural Low-Degree Filtering (Neural LoFi), a recently proposed layer-wise spectral surrogate for feature learning, to capture this interaction. Starting from the exact backpropagation gradients, we derive a local coupling between a neuron's incoming weights and its corresponding next-layer column. In a controlled small-initialization regime with smooth activations and fixed surroundings, these dynamics amplify singular modes of a cross-layer correlation operator. Each growing mode pairs an earlier feature with an upper-layer response through shared neuron coefficients. This motivates a backward-coupling algorithm in which upper-layer sensitivities generate sample-dependent effective labels for earlier spectral steps, while corrected features refine upward transmission. A function-space variational principle characterizes the selected feature-response pairs by maximizing the label correlation of their product under kernel-norm constraints. For three-layer networks, we derive self-consistent continuous-time dynamics for the filtered hidden-layer features, the activation kernels, and the network output under the proposed backward coupling. In a hierarchical multi-index model, we establish a feature-recovery separation: backward coupling recovers lower-layer directions invisible to the original forward label-weighted statistic. The linear specialization recovers residual-dependent singular-mode dynamics, while paired modes provide a dynamical mechanism for linked low-rank covariance components consistent with the rainbow-network picture. Experiments with fully connected and convolutional networks on binary CIFAR-10 show improved accuracy over forward Neural LoFi at matched widths.
papers.title_ja: 後方結合によるニューラルLoFi：層間特徴学習のスペクトル理論
papers.summary_ja: 逆伝播における層間フィードバックを捉えるため、層別スペクトルサロゲートであるNeural LoFiを拡張した理論を提案する。後方結合アルゴリズムにより、上位層の感度から下位層への効果的ラベルを生成し、特徴と応答のペアを最適化する。3層ネットワークにおける自己整合的な連続時間ダイナミクスを導出し、従来の前方統計では検出できない下位層の特徴方向を回復できることを示す。CIFAR-10での実験により、同幅のネットワークにおいて前方Neural LoFiを上回る精度が確認された。

papers.title: StackGen3D: Stable 3D Block Stack Generation from Multiview Silhouettes
papers.summary: Generating physically stable 3D structures from visual specifications requires resolving geometric ambiguity while accounting for physical interactions among objects. We present StackGen3D, a framework for generating stable block assemblies conditioned on a given block inventory and three orthographic silhouettes. Our approach consists of two stages. First, we develop a physics-informed graph neural network (PI-GNN) that models support relations between blocks and serves as a fast stability predictor for curating a diverse dataset of stable structures. Second, we train a conditional flow-matching model on this dataset to capture the multimodal distribution of block configurations consistent with the target silhouettes. At inference time, lightweight geometric selection and refinement reduce inter-block penetration without physics simulation. Preliminary experiments show that the PI-GNN generalizes from simple stacks to complex structures substantially better than a parameter-matched multilayer perceptron. For structure generation, Best-of-10 selection improves physical stability from 45.3% to 72.4% while achieving a silhouette IoU of 0.970. These results highlight the potential of combining relational physical reasoning, scalable data curation, and conditional generative modeling for creative 3D assembly. Project website: [https://ripl.github.io/StackGen3D-web/](https://ripl.github.io/StackGen3D-web/)

papers.title: ENCL: Enabling Efficient Neuromorphic Continual Learning with Local Learning Rule and Sub-Network Freezing Strategy
papers.summary: Continual learning (CL) in neural networks is a promising learning approach for updating the knowledge of deployed systems based on new data encountered at run time, that have not been learned during the offline training phase. To enable their power/energy-efficient CL processing, neuromorphic continual learning (NCL) concept with sparse event-based operations have recently been introduced. However, state-of-the-art NCL methods typically employ the memory-hungry data/experience replay, coupled with costly global learning rule (i.e., backpropagation-based surrogate gradient). To address these limitations, we propose ENCL, a novel methodology that enables efficient NCL by employing a lightweight local learning rule and sub-network freezing strategy. ENCL leverages the temporally- and spatially-local learning rule to perform efficient credit assignment for training new tasks, alleviating the expensive cost of global learning rule. ENCL also employs a sub-network freezing strategy based on the given tasks to avoid the needs for network architecture expansion, hence further improving the efficiency and scalability of the NCL training process. To efficiently support this, we train each task with a small number of epochs as well as adjusted learning rate and timestep. Experiment results on task-incremental learning (TIL) scenario show that, our ENCL consistently achieves strong performance across different datasets as compared to state-of-the-art works. Specifically, ENCL achieves competitive accuracy comparable to that of the state-of-the-art data/experience replay, while reducing memory cost by up to 88%, NCL training time by up to 51%, average power consumption by up to 40%, and energy consumption by up to 65% across different benchmarking datasets (i.e., Split MNIST, Split Fashion MNIST, Split CIFAR-10, and Split CIFAR-100).
papers.title_ja: ENCL：局所学習則とサブネットワーク凍結戦略による効率的なニューロモフィック継続学習の実現

papers.title: Neural Disjunctive Normal Forms for Learning Exact Rank Filters
papers.summary: Gradient-based learning of morphological operators is hindered by locally sparse derivatives with respect to the structuring elements. We develop a method for learning rank filters that retains exact operator evaluation while distributing the derivatives across the window. Using threshold decomposition, we construct a neural disjunctive normal form representation and establish a sufficient condition for exactness with integer-valued images and structuring elements. We then derive a smooth surrogate from the unique root of a smooth threshold equation. Implicit differentiation gives closed-form derivatives with normalised local weights, whose distribution is controlled by a smoothing parameter. These derivatives are used in a straight-through procedure: the forward pass evaluates the exact rank filter, while the backward pass uses the surrogate. For fixed ranks, the procedure learns real-valued structuring elements of any rank filter, including the median, and extends to compositions, infima, and suprema of rank filters. Experiments on image denoising using MNIST and Fashion-MNIST and retinal vessel segmentation show that, starting from a generic random initialisation, the proposed approach consistently improves performance over training with exact subgradients in every setting. In image denoising, our best network also outperforms smooth morphological networks in all settings. On vessel segmentation, the learned erosions recover structuring elements that fit the vessels, as theoretically expected, whereas most of those trained with exact subgradients remain close to their initialisation.

papers.title: A Globally Convergent Newton Method for Nonsmooth Optimization in the absence of Smooth Surrogates
papers.summary: We propose a globally convergent Newton method for convex composite optimization problems with polyhedral regularizers. The method rests on the observation that the proximal gradient step yields not only a new point but also a subgradient, which determines the face on which the linearization of the regularizer is exact. Minimizing a second-order model of the objective over this face produces a Newton direction that involves no generalized second-order information about the regularizer and is a descent direction for the objective itself. The method is therefore globalized by an Armijo line search on the original objective which, unlike forward-backward envelope techniques, requires only evaluations of the smooth component. We establish global convergence and local quadratic convergence to tilt-stable minimizers without any nondegeneracy condition, and show that the unit step is always accepted when the smooth component is quadratic, which yields a line-search-free method. The subproblems require only projections onto faces, which are explicit for the Lasso and nonnegative least squares and computable in linear time for the fused Lasso. Numerical experiments show that the method compares favorably with state-of-the-art solvers.

papers.title: Autoregressive Multimodal Anomaly Detection with Large Language Models for Microservice Systems
papers.summary: Microservice systems have become a dominant architecture for large-scale cloud applications, enabling rapid deployment and elastic scaling. However, ensuring the reliability and availability of microservice systems critically relies on effective anomaly detection, as failures and performance anomalies can quickly propagate across services and severely impact end-to-end system behavior. Existing multimodal anomaly detection approaches for microservice systems often struggle with two fundamental limitations: (i) the neglect of modality-specific characteristics in favor of cross-modality fusion, and (ii) the "identity-shortcut" problem that affects the feature reconstruction process. To address these issues, we propose LLMMAD, an autoregressive multimodal anomaly detection framework for microservice systems based on Large Language Models (LLMs). Initially, to reconcile cross-modality fusion with modality-specific preservation, LLMMAD embeds and recombines multimodal data into a unified sequence for LLM processing to model inter-modality relationships, while employing modality-wise reconstruction heads to retain modality-specific information. Subsequently, to eliminate the identity-shortcut, we implement a prediction-driven autoregressive objective, under which the model predicts future states rather than copies current inputs. Finally, we conduct extensive experiments on three real-world datasets. The results demonstrate that LLMMAD consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods, achieving F1-score improvements of 3.1%, 1.4%, and 0.9%, respectively, thereby providing a more reliable solution for microservice monitoring.

papers.title: A Mathematical Theory of the Jacobian Lens
papers.summary: Recent work from Anthropic introduced a new interpretability tool, called the Jacobian lens (J-lens, Gurnee et al., 2026). This method identified linear directions in the hidden states of frontier language models that had properties reminiscent of working memory-like representations. However, it is unclear what mechanistic properties of such features make them detectable to the J-lens. To this end, we introduce a mathematical theory of the J-lens, and show that it preferentially identifies coherent features -- directions that act like leading, spatially coherent Lyapunov modes. Small perturbations along these directions amplify across layers, remain roughly constant across token positions, and are consistent across different contexts. While we are agnostic to whether these properties are necessarily associated with a ``Global Workspace'', the analytically derived preferences of the J-lens nevertheless explain prior empirical applied to both model classes. We validate our analysis on a Bayes filter and a toy transformer, each optimally predicting next tokens emitted from a Hidden Markov Model (HMM). We show how modulating task parameters that change the coherence of features in the Bayes filter correspondingly and predictively modulates the response of the J-lens . We also introduce of a family of J-lenses built to emphasize different temporal scales of information processing in LLMs, which we call $\omega$-J-lenses.
papers.title_ja: ヤコビアンレンズの数学的理論

papers.title: Does LeWorldModel Preserve Local Action Geometry?
papers.summary: We examine how closely pretrained LeWorldModel (LeWM) reproduces the effects of small action changes. Using matched simulator and model responses, we measure action sensitivity with Gram matrices at three perturbation scales. Across nearly a thousand states from Reacher and OGBench Cube, the most sensitive action directions differ by median angles of about $36^\circ$ and $42^\circ$, respectively, at the smallest scale. Increasing the perturbation tenfold reduces median normalized Gram discrepancy by roughly 70\% on Reacher and 47\% on Cube. Geometry measured in pixels and embeddings varies more across scales than the chosen physical-state geometry. On held-out directions, environment Grams achieve median embedding response errors of 17\% and 28\%, compared with 26\% and 38\% for an isotropic reference with the same trace. LeWM's errors are higher at this scale. These findings support scale-specific evaluation of action sensitivity; its effect on control remains an open question.
papers.title_ja: LeWorldModelは局所的なアクション幾何学を保持しているか？

papers.title: Cognitively Constrained Partners for Zero-Shot Coordination in Real-Time Partitioned Control
papers.summary: Effective human-machine teaming requires agents that coordinate with unpredictable human partners. Reinforcement learning from live human feedback or large behavioural datasets is expensive, while purely simulated training overfits to artificial conventions and fails at Zero-Shot Coordination with real people. We propose a framework for training teaming agents against Cognitively Constrained Partners: simulated partners whose diversity emerges from procedural constraints grounded in human physiological literature, specifically reaction delays and perceptual limitations, rather than from reward shaping or historical training checkpoints. In a modified Lunar Lander environment, we report preliminary evidence that these partners play more like real people than unconstrained agents do, and that agents trained against them match the strongest cross-play baselines while being the only ones whose performance does not depend on how their training partners were generated. We also describe a human-participant study designed so that its rankings can be compared directly against cross-play, testing how well that standard evaluation predicts real human-agent teaming.
papers.title_ja: リアルタイム分割制御におけるゼロショット協調のための認知制約付きパートナー

papers.title: See What I Need, Dream What I Want: A Navigation Foundation Model on a Self-Constructed Representation Space
papers.summary: What visual representation should a navigation policy act on? Navigation policies built on vision foundation models largely leave representation design to the encoders' pretraining objectives. We present RepresentNav, a navigation foundation model built on a self-constructed representation space: a visual representation constructed by the policy's own objectives from vision foundation models. RepresentNav builds this space with Representation Residuals, a compact three-layer transformer that attends over features spanning the full depth of multiple complementary vision foundation models, so that the policy learns to see what it needs for navigation. In the same space it dreams what it wants: before every action a latent chain-of-thought predicts the representation of the scene a moment ahead. The dream is trained end-to-end with the policy as a joint-embedding predictive architecture (JEPA), with a next-representation prediction loss and a regularizer on its targets. RepresentNav sets a new state of the art on VLNVerse, VLN-CE R2R, EVT-Bench, and two point-goal benchmarks, and its gains carry over to a physical robot amid clutter and moving people. On VLNVerse fine-grained, RepresentNav achieves 83.80% success, outperforming the previous state of the art by 20.05 percentage points, and on EVT-Bench distracted tracking it reaches 85.5% with a single camera (+10.1). With the same encoders, the self-constructed space clearly outperforms concatenating their outputs and learns to weight their layers unevenly, and a dream in it cuts collisions by a quarter. A single dreamed latent decodes into the depth, semantics, and 3D occupancy of the scene a moment ahead, more accurately than pretrained encoders applied to the real future frame, although occupancy is never supervised, and the rollout tracks the robot's own motion over the next second: the dream emerges as a compact latent world model.

papers.title: Early learning in large residual networks
papers.summary: We study the early training dynamics of nonlinear residual networks with blocks of zero hidden layers as a model of more general residual networks. We analyze networks in a sequential limit where first width and depth diverge, then the number of training data points diverges, and finally the input dimension diverges. This is a more refined setup compared to the typical mean-field theory analysis in which depth and width diverge but the number of training datapoints and input dimension are fixed. Our main technical result is a diagrammatic computation of both the network output and the hidden representations after the few steps of gradient descent in terms of the statistics of inner products of inputs from the training set. One of our principle conceptual findings is a negative result: in the limit of large input dimension the network output can learn only a linear function of its inputs early in training since higher learned monomials are more and more suppressed in the input dimension and vanish in the large dimension limit. This suggests that mean-field limits of ResNets are surprisingly rigid in the regime of high input dimension and may not be sufficient toy models for understanding feature learning. Finally, we investigate how to ensure hyperparameter transfer for the learning rate as a function of dataset size and input dimension. We test our predictions numerically and find excellent agreement with our theory.

papers.title: Not All Retained Clients Are Equal: Client Selection for Federated Unlearning
papers.summary: Federated unlearning (FU) aims to remove a designated target client's influence from a trained model without the prohibitive cost of retraining from scratch. Existing methods largely treat unlearning as a post-hoc, stateless operation, overlooking that client influence is path-dependent: contributions made during training, particularly during critical learning periods (CLPs), can have disproportionate and persistent effects. Moreover, knowledge overlap and intermittent client availability make relying on all retained clients inefficient and impractical. We introduce PDF, a path-dependent client-selection framework based on the insight that retained clients are not equally valuable for unlearning. During training, PDF maintains lightweight, target-agnostic, CLP-weighted histories summarizing each client's accumulated update direction and global-model alignment. Upon an unlearning request, these histories identify and rank retained clients that are globally informative yet weakly coupled to the target, enabling retraining-based unlearning with only the top-$k$ clients over a small number of rounds. Experiments on FMNIST, CIFAR-10, and CIFAR-100 under IID and non-IID settings show that PDF achieves effective forgetting and strong retained utility with substantially fewer retained clients. In particular, PDF achieves $0\%$ forgetting accuracy with retraining-like MIA AUC on non-IID CIFAR-10, improves retained accuracy by up to $6.91$ percentage points over the strongest competing FU baseline on CIFAR-100, and reduces communication by approximately $69\%$ and computation by $57$--$61\%$ relative to Retrain.
papers.title_ja: 保持クライアントはすべて等価ではない：連邦アンラーニングにおけるクライアント選択
papers.summary_ja: 本論文は、連邦アンラーニング（FU）において、クライアントの影響が学習経路に依存する（path-dependent）という洞察に基づき、効率的なクライアント選択フレームワーク「PDF」を提案する。訓練中に軽量な履歴情報を維持し、アンラーニング要求時にターゲットクライアントとの結合が弱く、かつグローバルに情報量の高いクライアントを特定・ランキングする。これにより、上位k個のクライアントのみを用いた再訓練ベースのアンラーニングを実現し、通信量と計算量を大幅に削減しながら、忘却精度と保持ユーティリティを両立させる。実験では、競合手法と比較して保持精度の向上と計算コストの大幅な低減を示した。

papers.title: PaperScorer: How Predictable Is Paper Acceptance?
papers.summary: Automated research is largely evaluated by benchmark performance, but the value of research rarely reduces to a single score. Humans judge a work's holistic contribution through peer review, which is hard to model because it is noisy and depends on many factors. However, what if, given only the paper, we could predict its peer-review decision directly? We introduce PaperScorer, a family of models that predict a paper's accept or reject decision from its extracted text or page screenshots, training only on the decision after removing author identity and formatting shortcuts. Vision models are the most predictive (68% accuracy on ICLR papers and 77% on ML papers from arXiv), beating text-only and frontier reasoning models. Unlike plain text, page images retain figures, layout, and presentation. This signal is robust, surviving smaller models and even compressing the whole paper into a single image. But accurate predictions are not evenly spread. PaperScorer is strongest on the lowest and highest rated papers, while papers rated in the middle stay unpredictable for our models and frontier systems alike. Additionally, its confidence is calibrated, so its most confident predictions are also its most accurate. Overall, PaperScorer shows how much of the decision a paper carries on its own, marking a first step toward AI-driven research evaluation.
papers.title_ja: PaperScorer: 論文の採択はどの程度予測可能か？
papers.summary_ja: 本論文は、論文のテキストやページ画像からピアレビューの採択・却下判定を予測するモデル群 PaperScorer を提案する。視覚モデルが最も予測精度が高く、ICLR 論文で 68%、arXiv の ML 論文で 77% の精度を達成した。予測は極端な評価（高評価・低評価）の論文で強く、中間評価の論文は予測困難であることが示された。また、モデルの信頼度は較正されており、最も自信のある予測が最も正確であることも確認された。

papers.title: Emergent Cooperative Thermoregulation in Lunar Swarm Robotics
papers.summary: Swarms of small robots are an attractive way to survey lunar caves and lava tubes. Missions such as NASA's CADRE will fly cooperating rovers for distributed mapping, but only in daylight. The 354 h lunar night drops the surface towards 95 K, and the radioisotope heaters that let single rovers survive it cannot be supplied at swarm scale. In this study we investigate whether a swarm can instead use its own members as thermal shielding. We train one policy, shared by all twenty robots, by reinforcement learning with an evolution-strategies estimator. The policy receives a single reward, once, at the end of the night: the mean temperature of the five coldest robots. Nothing in that reward refers to position, spacing, exposure or motion. Two behaviors nonetheless emerge. The swarm aggregates, and robots circulate between the sheltered core and the exposed rim, the same pair of behaviors with which emperor penguins survive the Antarctic winter. We measure the survival threshold, the smallest stored energy per robot at which every robot is still alive at sunrise. Across ten runs it is 155.6 +/- 1.3 pcm-h, where one pcm-h is 7.2 kJ of stored heat. That is 37% below a motionless huddle and within 13% of a physics-based lower bound, and at a budget where the motionless huddle loses six robots, every robot survives. The behavior needs no shared spatial reference and no robot-robot contact, and transfers from twenty robots to forty without retraining.
papers.title_ja: 月面スウォームロボティクスにおける創発的協調熱調節
papers.summary_ja: 月面の極端な低温環境下で、小型ロボット群が互いを熱遮蔽として利用する協調行動を強化学習により実現した。進化戦略を用いた報酬設計により、位置や接触を明示しないまま、ペンギンのような集団と循環行動が創発する。この手法により、静止した集団より37%少ないエネルギーで全ロボットの生存を達成し、40台への拡張でも再学習なしで動作することが示された。

papers.title: Forecasting Associations, Not Interventions: A Preregistered Causal Audit of Covariate-Aware Time Series Foundation Models
papers.summary: Covariate-aware time series foundation models (TSFMs) accept a future path for a control variable and return a forecast, inviting what-if queries. The query is interventional; the models are trained on observational data. We determine whether their answers are the conditional slope $\partial E[Y|X]$ or the interventional effect $\partial E[Y|do(X)]$, at three levels. Theory: a Bayes-optimal observational predictor answers interventional queries associationally unless the adjustment set is available and used; for in-context least squares we derive the resulting confounding gap -- a model's effect estimate under an observational minus under a randomized context -- in closed form, a parameter-free reference line. Behaviour: on a preregistered grid with exact counterfactual ground truth, Chronos-2, TiRex-2, TabPFN-TS and TimesFM-2.5 all track this line ($R^2$ 0.90-1.00) and respond more confounded than regression itself (slopes 1.3-1.8), on linear and nonlinear structural models. Pairs of models with identical observational laws prove this is not an identifiability limit: when the effect is identifiable, least squares recovers 100% of the true effect difference, Chronos-2 75%, TiRex-2 34%. Representation: linear probes decode the data-generating regime (94-96%) and the true effect ($R^2$ 0.7-0.9) from embeddings that the forecasts ignore. On two physical systems with randomized actuators, pretrained models under-respond by 2-5x and ignore in-window confounding. Minutes of interventional post-training on 3,000 synthetic series cut the gap by up to 83% and transfer outside the training prior. Its forecasting cost is a replay-distribution effect: replaying the model's own pretraining prior cuts it from +47% to +10% MASE, and with low-rank adaptation yields a recipe meeting the preregistered criterion over three seeds (52-61% gap reduction at +1-3% cost) while improving the DoTime benchmark.
papers.title_ja: 介入ではなく関連の予測：共変量対応時系列基盤モデルの事前登録因果監査
papers.summary_ja: 共変量対応時系列基盤モデル（TSFM）が観測データから学習した際に、介入効果（what-if）を正しく推定できるかを理論・行動・表現の3レベルで検証した。理論的に導出された混同ギャップの基準線に対し、Chronos-2等の主要モデルは回帰分析よりも大きな混同バイアスを持つことを示した。また、埋め込み表現からは真の因果効果が復号可能であるが、予測出力では無視されていることを発見した。最後に、少数の合成データによる介入的ポストトレーニングにより、このギャップを最大83%削減しつつ予測精度を維持する手法を提案した。

papers.title: FLORA: An Open Model Suite for Scaling Robotics Data Engines
papers.summary: The life-cycle of robotics foundation models crucially depends on data labels. Outcome reward labels are needed for monitoring real-world deployments. Process reward labels are needed during RL post-training. Timestamped captions are needed for filtering and balancing pretraining data. We present Flora, an industrial-quality data engine used for training GR00T models, that simultaneously covers these capabilities. Flora achieves SOTA scores on the captioning benchmark WGO-Bench and reward benchmarks RoboReward and Robometer. On internal benchmarks it is competitive with GPT-6 Astra while beating other frontier models. The model is substantially cheaper than API-based alternatives, roughly 125 times cheaper than GPT-6 Astra. Florais battle tested at scale, labeling 200,000 hours of data per day across 512 GB300s. By open-sourcing our data engine, we enable researchers to scale custom robotics datasets and explore emerging applications such as physical auto-research and human-to-robot transfer.
papers.title_ja: FLORA: ロボティクスデータエンジンのスケーリングのためのオープンモデルスイート

papers.title: Collaborative In-Context Learning for Indoor Radio Map Estimation
papers.summary: Indoor radio map estimation (RME) is essential for wireless applications such as coverage planning, localization, and network deployment. However, most existing methods follow a supervised learning paradigm that requires costly labeled data and task-specific model training. Moreover, indoor environments involve privacy-sensitive information, such as building layouts and structures, that often cannot be centralized. To address these challenges, we make the first attempt to formulate indoor RME as a collaborative in-context learning (ICL) problem. We propose Poly-Ripple, a framework in which multiple clients perform ICL using large autoregressive vision models (LAVMs) without model updates. Each client is prompted by its private demonstrations and predicts the radio map for the same scene query. To capture the causal structure of wireless propagation outward from the transmitter (Tx), we adopt ripple-ordered autoregressive modeling. We further introduce importance-aware aggregation to exploit heterogeneous contextual knowledge distributed across clients under the context length constraint. We provide theoretical analysis and conduct extensive experiments on a public indoor RME benchmark. The experimental results show that Poly-Ripple consistently outperforms representative ICL baselines, while aligning with our theoretical analysis.
papers.title_ja: 屋内無線マップ推定のための協調的インコンテキスト学習
papers.summary_ja: 屋内無線マップ推定（RME）を協調的インコンテキスト学習（ICL）問題として定式化し、モデル更新なしで推論を行うフレームワーク「Poly-Ripple」を提案する。複数のクライアントがプライベートなデモデータを用いて大規模自己回帰ビジョンモデル（LAVM）をプロンプトし、送信源からの因果構造を捉えるリップル順序の自己回帰モデリングを採用する。さらに、コンテキスト長制約下でクライアント間の異質な文脈知識を活用する重要度認識集約法を導入し、理論解析と実験により既存ベースラインを上回る性能を実証した。

papers.title: ConsMSA: Semantic Distribution Consistency Learning for Multimodal Sentiment Analysis
papers.summary: Multimodal sentiment analysis (MSA) aims to predict human sentiments by integrating signals from different modalities such as text, video, and audio. However, raw multimodal sequences often suffer from semantic inconsistency--exhibiting redundancy or conflicts within and across modalities--which hinders robust understanding and increases computational cost. To this end, we introduce ConsMSA, which explicitly formalizes semantic distribution consistency across both $\textit{intra}$- and $\textit{inter}$-modality, providing a consistency-aware mechanism for robust and efficient multimodal sentiment prediction. Specifically, ConsMSA projects multimodal token features into a shared sentiment space to compute an Intra- and Inter-modality Consistency Score ($I^2CS$). By coupling this score with predictive relevance, we formulate consistency-aware importance signals that are utilized: (i) as a consistency regularizer to align latent distributions during training, (ii) to derive semantic-aware weights for adaptive multimodal token reweighting, and (iii) as a practical criterion to prune redundant or conflicting tokens. Extensive experiments on CMU-MOSI, CMU-MOSEI, and CH-SIMS demonstrate that ConsMSA achieves state-of-the-art performance while remaining robust under aggressive token compression--retaining only 10% of tokens yields comparable accuracy. These results establish semantic distribution consistency as a promising foundation for synergizing predictive robustness with computational efficiency.
papers.title_ja: ConsMSA: マルチモーダル感情分析のための意味分布一貫性学習
papers.summary_ja: マルチモーダル感情分析におけるモダリティ間・内の意味的不整合を解決し、計算効率と予測精度を両立させる手法 ConsMSA を提案する。共有された感情空間にトークンを射影し、一貫性スコアを用いて冗長なトークンを剪定するメカニズムを導入した。このアプローチにより、トークンを 10% に圧縮しても同等の精度を維持できることを示し、計算コストの大幅削減を実現した。

papers.title: Rethinking Multi-View Fusion for Urban Representation Learning
papers.summary: Urban region representation learning encodes heterogeneous urban signals, such as mobility flows, points of interest, and land-use patterns, into unified embeddings for downstream tasks, including check-in prediction, crime forecasting, and service demand estimation. Existing approaches rely on globally shared fusion and joint optimization, implicitly assuming uniform modality importance and naturally balanced multi-objective training. However, urban data is inherently heterogeneous. Our empirical analysis reveals two structural issues: (i) modality utility varies markedly across regions, causing static fusion to overemphasize signals from certain modalities; and (ii) heterogeneous objectives exhibit persistent gradient imbalance, causing representational bias and unstable training. We present PRISM, a self-adjusting framework for adaptive multi-view learning. PRISM adapts sparse MoE routing to learn region-specific view allocations, while a PID (Proportional Integral Derivative)-inspired regulation mechanism mitigates gradient conflicts during optimization. Experiments on three large-scale urban datasets show that PRISM achieves competitive performance compared with strong multi-view baselines, while providing more stable optimization behavior and more balanced region representations.
papers.title_ja: 都市表現学習におけるマルチビュー融合の再考
papers.summary_ja: 都市データにおける異種モダリティの融合において、地域ごとの有用性の偏りや勾配のアンバランスが学習の不安定さを招く問題を指摘する。提案手法PRISMは、スパースMoEルーティングにより地域ごとに適応的なビュー配分を行い、PID制御インスパイアされた機構で勾配競合を緩和する。3つの大規模都市データセットでの実験により、既存手法と比較して安定した最適化とバランスの取れた表現学習が実現できることを示した。

papers.title: The Path to NDE 4.0: A Review of Algorithms, Techniques, and Strategies for Autonomous Inspection
papers.summary: Non-Destructive Inspection (NDI) is a cornerstone of modern quality assurance, critical for ensuring the safety and reliability of infrastructure and manufactured components without causing damage. This paper presents a comprehensive review of the current NDI landscape, analyzing the field through four distinct lenses, namely, computational algorithms, physical techniques, industrial applications, and research objectives. We synthesize a broad range of academic literature to illustrate the rapid evolution from manual, analog interpretation to a digitized, data-centric paradigm known as NDE 4.0. Our analysis highlights the dominance of ultrasound and visual inspection as primary physical techniques, while revealing a significant shift toward deep learning and generative models for automated defect recognition. Despite these technological strides, the industry faces critical bottlenecks, notably the scarcity of standardized open-access datasets and the "black box" nature of AI models, which hinders widespread adoption. By charting these developments and identifying key research gaps, such as the need for explainable AI (XAI) and standardized digital twin protocols, this review offers a strategic roadmap for future research. It concludes that the future of NDI research should focus on the successful integration of intelligent, autonomous fusion of inspection data with advanced sensor technologies into asset lifecycle management.
papers.title_ja: NDE 4.0への道：自律検査のためのアルゴリズム、技術、戦略のレビュー
papers.summary_ja: 本論文は、非破壊検査（NDI）分野における「NDE 4.0」への移行を包括的にレビューする。深層学習や生成モデルを用いた欠陥認識の自動化が進む一方で、標準化されたオープンデータセットの不足やAIモデルのブラックボックス性が産業導入のボトルネックとなっていることを指摘する。説明可能AI（XAI）やデジタルツインプロトコルの必要性を強調し、センサー技術と資産ライフサイクル管理の統合に向けた戦略的ロードマップを提示する。

papers.title: Scaling Transformer Energy-based Models For High Quality Image Synthesis
papers.summary: Energy-Based Models (EBMs) are a flexible class of generative models that decouple probabilistic modeling from the generation process. This decoupling directly enables compositional generation and inference-time scaling, where sample quality can be refined simply by increasing sampling steps. However, severe challenges in high-dimensional sampling and training instabilities with deep architectures have restricted EBMs to low-dimensional regimes. To resolve these bottlenecks, we introduce the Transformer Energy-Based Model (TEM), a scalable transformer energy function operating entirely within a latent space. On top of this backbone, we extract energies at multiple layers and sum them, composing complementary constraints from local texture to global semantics. Furthermore, two components make this high-quality at scale: Positive Representation Alignment (PRA), which supervises TEM's intermediate representations with a vision foundation model, and advanced sampling strategies that improve sample quality at inference. TEM-XL achieves an FID-50K of 3.82 on class-conditional ImageNet 256$\times$256 without classifier-free guidance, showing that a contrastive EBM can generate high-fidelity images. On ImageNet 512$\times$512, TEM achieves an FID-50K of 8.24, demonstrating that the approach scales to higher resolution. We further validate the core promises of EBMs: compositional generation, zero-shot inpainting, and out-of-distribution detection.
papers.title_ja: 高品質画像合成のためのTransformerエネルギーベースモデルのスケーリング
papers.summary_ja: エネルギーベースモデル（EBM）の訓練不安定性と高次元サンプリングの課題を解決するため、潜在空間内で動作するTransformerベースのエネルギー関数TEMを提案する。視覚基盤モデルによる中間表現の監督（PRA）と多層エネルギーの合成により、ImageNet 256x256でFID-50K 3.82という高品質な画像生成を実現した。また、推論時のステップ増加による品質向上や、ゼロショットインペインティング、分布外検出などEBM固有の柔軟性を検証している。

papers.title: Concept Acupuncturist: An Efficient and Precise Concept Erasure Method for Diffusion Models via Sparse Autoencoders
papers.summary: Diffusion-based image generation models produce high-quality images but may generate harmful or policy-violating content, motivating machine unlearning (MU) to selectively remove target concepts while preserving general capabilities. However, existing MU approaches often struggle with the distributed and entangled nature of concept representations, leading to inefficient optimization and imprecise edits when applied through large-scale fine-tuning over full diffusion trajectories. To bridge this gap, we propose Concept Acupuncturist (ConceptACP), a novel MU framework that integrates interpretability-guided analysis with inference-free fine-tuning for efficient and precise concept removal. By establishing mappings between semantic concepts and cross-attention blocks in the U-Net denoiser and localizing the most concept-relevant block for targeted optimization, ConceptACP avoids full diffusion trajectory optimization, thereby improving fine-tuning efficiency. To mitigate concept entanglement, we propose a feature-level correction mechanism based on Sparse Autoencoders (SAEs), where SAE-derived sparse, semantically meaningful feature activations are manipulated to construct targeted correction signals, which are then projected back to the output space of the corresponding block and used as supervision for precise concept removal. Consequently, ConceptACP eliminates the need for external inference-time modules while achieving efficient and fine-grained unlearning. Instantiated on SDXL-Turbo, ConceptACP improves the forgetting success rate by 36.34 percentage points in the standard one-step generation setting on average over the best-performing baseline, while preserving image quality and prompt fidelity, and generalizes effectively across other Stable Diffusion backbones. Our code is available at https://github.com/Eran-Xia/ConceptACP.

papers.summary_ja: 拡散モデルにおける機械的忘却（Machine Unlearning）の課題に対し、解釈可能性分析と推論不要なファインチューニングを統合した新フレームワーク「Concept Acupuncturist」を提案する。U-Netデノイザー内のクロスアテンションブロックと意味的コンセプトのマッピングを確立し、最も関連性の高いブロックを特定することで、全軌道の最適化を回避し効率を向上させる。さらに、疎自動符号化器（SAE）を用いた特徴レベルの補正メカニズムにより、概念の絡み合いを緩和し、精密な概念除去を実現する。SDXL-Turboでの実験により、既存ベースライン比で忘却成功率を36.34ポイント向上させつつ、画像品質とプロンプト忠実度を維持することを示した。

papers.title: Exact Global Minimax Risk near Nonidentification
papers.summary: We study squared-error estimation when a nuisance parameter is unidentified on a submodel but affects a target that vanishes there. For models with higher-order profile expansions, we give sufficient conditions under which the largest critical-path minimax risk is the exact asymptotic minimax risk over the full parameter space. An efficient observable feature, negligible calibration error and stable recovery yield one estimator attaining the leading constant uniformly, with the profile coordinates unknown. The estimator uses calibration estimates, a local feature mean and an empirical recovery feature. The constant is expressed through a bounded-normal decision problem. We verify the conditions in two models. In centered Gaussian logistic errors-in-variables regression with one surrogate and two unknown variances, we determine the fifth-order global coefficient risk and its exact constant. A sparse extension separates variance-decomposition uncertainty from direction estimation and specifies when the scalar constant is preserved. In a degree-balanced replicated-network model, we determine the sixth-order global edge-contrast risk when block proportions are unknown. Triangles identify a parameter combination; a bowtie supplies the additional information needed for the contrast.
papers.title_ja: 非識別領域付近における厳密なグローバルミニマックスリスク

papers.title: Towards Adversarially Robust Multigraph Neural Networks for Financial Crime Analysis
papers.summary: Financial transaction networks are naturally represented as multigraphs, where repeated transactions between the same pair of accounts are modeled as distinct edges. Recently proposed multigraph neural network architectures leverage this structure explicitly to achieve a strong performance on anti-money laundering (AML) tasks. However, their robustness to adversaries that manipulate transaction structures to evade detection remains largely unexplored. We present the first scalable framework for structural attacks and adversarial training of multigraph neural networks using node-edge incidence matrices, adapting projected gradient descent and projected randomized block coordinate descent methods to optimize structural perturbations over such matrices. We further introduce a cycle-based regularizer that penalizes changes in the global counts of directed 2- and 3-cycles, providing a structural measure of attack plausibility. Experiments on synthetic pattern-detection and realistic AML datasets show that our learned attacks substantially outperform non-learnable perturbation baselines in reducing detection performance (PR-AUC), while adversarial training consistently improves robustness against these attacks. These results demonstrate that multigraph neural networks are vulnerable to learned structural attacks and that adversarial training provides an effective defense. Our code is available at https://github.com/denheijmans/robust_multignn.
papers.title_ja: 金融犯罪分析のための敵対的ロバストなマルチグラフニューラルネットワークへ
papers.summary_ja: 本論文は、反マネーロンダリング（AML）タスクで高性能を示すマルチグラフニューラルネットワーク（MultiGNN）の敵対的頑健性を初めて体系的に調査する。ノード・エッジ入射行列を用いた構造攻撃フレームワークを提案し、射影勾配降下法やランダム化ブロック座標降下法を適応して構造摂動を最適化する手法を開発した。さらに、有向2-3サイクルのグローバルカウント変化をペナルティとするサイクルベースの正則化項を導入し、攻撃の妥当性を構造面で評価する。実験により、学習された構造攻撃は既存ベースラインより検出性能を大幅に低下させ、敵対的訓練が有効な防御策であることを示した。

papers.title: Exposing Noise-Deficiency Signatures of Deep Learning-Based False Data Injection Attacks Through AC State Estimation
papers.summary: Deep learning (DL)-based false data injection (FDI) attacks can resemble normal measurements and evade both conventional bad data detection (BDD) and measurement-space data-driven detectors. This paper identifies a previously overlooked signature of such attacks in state-estimation (SE) residual space. The residuals of reconstruction-based DL attacks exhibit deficient stochastic variation, manifested as abnormally small residual energy and reduced directional dispersion. We establish the conditions under which this signature emerges and explain why the attacks carrying it can evade conventional BDD. We show that SE can reveal residual-space differences obscured by operating-state variation in measurement space. We then explain the origin of the signature through the noise-suppression mechanism of DL attack generation. A generator can learn the reproducible structure of historical measurements but cannot reproduce stochastic measurement components that are unpredictable from its input. This signature enables label-free detection using a simple two-sided test on the conventional BDD statistic, while the full residual vector can also be exploited when labeled attack samples are available. Experiments on the IEEE 14-bus and 118-bus AC systems show that the label-free test detects up to 99% of three representative DL attacks at a false-alarm rate comparable to that of BDD, which detects at most 5%. papers.title: Higher-order asymptotic formulae for periodic orbits of 3-dimensional volume-preserving Anosov flows and the Foulon conjecture
papers.summary: Let $X^t$ be a volume-preserving Anosov flow of class $C^7$ on a closed $3$-manifold. We consider a sequence of periodic orbits which shadow a homoclinic loop of a fixed periodic orbit $\gamma$, and derive higher-order asymptotic expansions for their periods $T_n$ and for the logarithms of their unstable multipliers $\log\lambda_n$. We give geometric interpretations of the coefficients in these expansions, in particular in terms of the Anosov cocycle (\`a la Hurder-Katok) and the longitudinal Anosov cocycle (\`a la Foulon-Hasselblatt), evaluated on $\gamma$. Following the idea of De Simoi-Leguil-Vinhage-Yang, we compare these asymptotics when volume is the measure of maximal entropy. In this case, the equilibrium-state characterizations of volume and the measure of maximal entropy synchronize periods and exponents: $\log\lambda_n=hT_n$. Matching the coefficients of the two asymptotic expansions forces the cohomology classes of both cocycles to vanish. Then the work of Foulon-Hasselblatt on the longitudinal Anosov cocycle, together with Foulon's work on the contact case, yields the Foulon Conjecture for flows of class $C^7$: if volume is the measure of maximal entropy, then, up to a finite cover, $X^t$ is smoothly conjugate either to a constant-roof suspension of a hyperbolic automorphism of the $2$-torus or to a finite cover of the constant-speed geodesic flow on a closed hyperbolic surface.

papers.title: Multi modal perceived conversation success prediction for spontaneous autistic and non-autistic dyadic interactions
papers.summary: Conversation success is important for communication, social bonds, and well-being and is often reduced in autistic-neurotypical conversations. Previous studies have predicted perceived conversation success using acoustic and lexical features in pediatric autism-enriched samples, or using nonverbal behavior in non-autistic group interactions. Other work has characterized prosodic, facial, motor, and turn-taking synchrony in autistic interactions, but has primarily targeted diagnostic classification or group differences. The present study instead predicts participant perceived conversation success from complementary articulatory, facial, acoustic-prosodic, and turn-taking measures across three spontaneous dyadic-interaction datasets including autistic and non autistic individuals. By leveraging multimodal features, we demonstrate that conversational success is inherently multidimensional and requires a multi-faceted analytical framework. Combining these complementary modalities offers the potential to improve prediction of perceived conversation success by capturing information unavailable from any single modality.

papers.title: Patronizing and Condescending Language Detection in English and Mandarin
papers.summary: Patronizing and condescending language (PCL) is a form of harmful language that belittles and assumes pity for vulnerable groups, reinforcing negative societal stereotypes. However, unlike overt hate speech, it is often difficult to detect, even for human judges. This paper proposes a system for the automated detection of PCL. Our first approach uses static word embeddings and a convolutional neural network for classification, while our second approach uses pre-trained BERT embeddings fine-tuned for the PCL task. Our second approach was considerably more successful, and achieved an F1 score of 0.528 over the development set.
